summary: M. D. Balasubrahmanyam worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at Savitribai Phule Pune University, where he also held a post attested in 1967.

M. G. Dhadphale is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000) and as editor of Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).

M. H. Krishna (1892–1947) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Maharaja's College, Mysore, the University of Madras, and UCL under Ernest Arthur Gardner, he served at Maharaja's College and the University of Mysore.

M. R. Raghava Varier specializes in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Calicut, Archaeological Survey of India, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, later serving as professor at the University of Calicut (~1976–1996).

M. S. A. Rao (1926–1985) worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye, later holding posts at Delhi, Syracuse, and the University of Pennsylvania.

M. S. Nagaraja Rao (1932–2011) was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Mysore and Savitribai Phule Pune universities, and held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, Karnatak University, and the Karnataka State Archaeology Department.

M. Seshagiri Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics. In 1899, he was attested as curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and professor of Sanskrit and comparative philology at Presidency University.

M. Shinoda is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Shinoda studied under Seiren Matsunami, having previously attended Agoura High School (~1991–1995) and Art Center College of Design (~1995–1998).

M. Yamunacharya worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied under Mysore Hiriyanna, Ardeshir Ruttonji Wadia, and Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, and served as professor in philosophy at Maharaja's College, Mysore.

M.L. Pattaratorn Chirapravati specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Educated at Silpakorn, Ohio State, and Cornell universities, she held posts at California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016), Silpakorn, Tsukuba, Sonoma State, Yale-NUS, and NTU.
Maanasa Visweswaran works in computational Indology. She is attested in 2026 as studying and holding an appointment as Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg.
Mabel Bode (1864–1922) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Bern, UCL, and in Paris, learning under T. W. Rhys Davids, Cecil Bendall, and others, and lectured at UCL and SOAS.

Mabel Haynes Bode (1864–1922) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at UCL and the University of Bern, including under T. W. Rhys Davids, and held posts at UCL and SOAS (~1917–1922).

Maciej Eder specializes in computational linguistics. He studied at the University of Breslau under Marcin Cieński and held posts at the University of the National Education Commission (~2008–2018) and the Institute of Polish Language (~2011).

Madeleine Biardeau (1922–2010) was an Indologist who worked on religious studies and philosophy. She studied at the École Normale Supérieure de Sèvres and University of Kerala, and served as a teacher at EPHE (~1956–1989).
Madhav M. Deshpande specializes in Indology and linguistics. A student of Ludo Rocher, he served as a professor at the University of Michigan (attested 1976 and 2006–2009).

Madhav Sadashiv Gore (1921–2010) studied at the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye and at the Columbia University School of Social Work. He later held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1997–2002).
Madhu Khanna is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She held posts at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, both attested in 2012.

Madhukar Anant Mehendale (1918–2020) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held posts as joint secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky (1927–2016) was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. A graduate of Fergusson College, he founded the Archeology Research Group in 1951 and held associate director and director emeritus posts at the American Institute of Indian Studies.
